text:
The most-asked question around Columbus isn't about the standings. It's whether Zach Werenski still wants to be there. Bleacher Report put him on a list of players likely to request a trade next, and The Hockey News asked whether he's reconsidering his commitment. Nothing in our facts says he has asked out, so treat it as speculation. But a 7-12-0 start is how that kind of speculation starts.

The losing is partly real. The Blue Jackets are winless in five, outscored 21-8, with 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that run and 46% on the season. They have also scored more than ten fewer goals than their chances earned. Injuries haven't helped: Conor Garland went on injured reserve, week to week, and Sean Monahan has been day to day with an upper-body injury, which broke up their line with Valeri Nichushkin. Behind the bench, Rick Bowness missed two games with a health issue, with Don Granato filling in, and NHL.com reported Bowness planned to rejoin the team on this road trip.

The goalie isn't the problem. Cam Talbot has saved 3.8 goals above expected over his last five starts. The Charlie Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger line has driven play (53% of the expected goals). Our playoff odds are 5%. What to watch is less the scoreboard than how long Werenski's name stays in those headlines.
